discovery: Prediction and experimental demonstration of anyons: quantum particles with fractional exchange statistics in two dimensions

nominees.name: Jan Myrheim
nominees.affiliation: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), Norway

subfield: Condensed matter physics / quantum statistics and topological phases
motivation: In 1977 Leinaas and Myrheim showed, from a careful analysis of the configuration space of identical particles, that quantum mechanics in two dimensions allows exchange statistics interpolating continuously between bosons and fermions. This deep insight, later named 'anyons', became the conceptual foundation for understanding the fractional quantum Hall effect, topological order and non-Abelian braiding, and underpins proposals for topologically protected quantum computation. For decades the braiding of anyons remained indirect. Manfra's ultra-high-mobility GaAs heterostructures and the Fabry-Perot interferometer developed in his group (Nakamura et al., Nature Physics 2020) provided the first direct observation of anyonic braiding phases at filling 1/3, consistent with the predicted fractional statistics, confirmed by complementary collider experiments. Together these contributions establish a genuinely new category of quantum particle, a fundamental extension of the spin-statistics picture that reshaped how physicists understand quantum matter.
